system_info.memtier_version: memtier_benchmark v=255.255.255 sha=272eeb64:0 bits=64 libevent=2.1.12-stable openssl=OpenSSL 3.0.13 30 Jan 2024 prometheus=yes

tuning.sweep_metric: SET+GET ops/sec at the run's datasize

memtier.key_pattern: R (uniform random) over the populated range

notes: maxmemory=0 (no memory cap) on HotKV, Redis, Valkey; Dragonfly kept its default cap (maxmemory 266 GB; its largest resident set in the run was 43 GB).
Persistence off everywhere (Redis/Valkey --save '' --appendonly no; Dragonfly --dbfilename= ). No server pays disk IO the others do not.
No server-specific tuning beyond thread count; see tuning.tuned_threads.
The read range is exactly the range populate filled, so reads hit ~100% and measure the value path rather than the nil path.

--distinct-client-seed: every client gets its own key sequence. Without it memtier seeds all clients identically and thousands of connections replay one key order, which manufactures cache locality no real workload has. Applied to every server equally.

corrections: 2026-10-09, after the run: the harness recorded 156 memtier threads per client box (the count derived from the server's cores) and 7,800 connections. memtier's own output for every run (raw/p30_4srv_raw.tgz, parts/*/*.json, configuration.threads) shows each client box ran 64 threads x 50 connections, 3,200 connections. threads_per_client_machine, total_connections_per_client_machine and system_info.bench_threads were corrected to match; the harness now records the threads each client box runs.

2026-10-09, after the run: the harness noted 'maxmemory=0 on every server'. Dragonfly reports a default cap (effective_config.maxmemory); the note was corrected to say so. The harness now builds the note from each server's reported maxmemory.
